input.rationale: Section 13.5 starts in the right place — Developments created solely by Corio are owned by Corio and Commerce One assigns any claim it would otherwise have (p0116) — and Section 2.8 correctly limits Commerce One to its own Software, which is acceptable. The failure is the carve-out: where Commerce One supports a Development on an ongoing basis, Commerce One "will retain all ownership rights, including intellectual property rights in the Developments", with no licence back to Corio. That is an effective transfer of our own hosting-integration IP to the vendor and sits in walk-away territory, and it fails the fallback because Corio is left with no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free right to use or modify code it created and paid for. The redline deletes only the carve-out, leaving Commerce One's pre-existing materials and the Software untouched. Two lesser points noted but not separately flagged: the agreement has no express Customer Data / hosted customer data ownership statement, and the final sentence of 13.5 leaves ownership of enhancements to the Software itself to future negotiation — both can be raised as drafting points if the counterparty reopens Section 13.

proposal.summary: Delete the carve-out in Section 13.5 that transfers ownership of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One where Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the carve-out that would give Commerce One ownership of Developments created solely by Corio simply because Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis, since we cannot assign our own IP to a vendor and there is no licence back. Commerce One's pre-existing materials and the Software itself remain its property under Sections 13.5 and 2.8; if ongoing support is the concern, we can instead grant Commerce One a licence to use and support those Developments.
